title: HelixScale Systems — partnership intro + integration scoping
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and HelixScale to explore reseller/onramp options, technical integration patterns (API, VPC, on-prem images), security/compliance requirements, and go-to-market mechanics. Agreed to run a small pilot (1-2 customers) and share security pack + preliminary SOW. Discussed SLA expectations, margin concerns, and technical feasibility for private deployments and dedicated GPU pools.
topics: HelixScale business model and target customers
Integration patterns: hosted API vs VPC peering vs on-prem package
Dedicated capacity / reserved GPU pools and autoscaling expectations
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs
Operational flows: billing, support, playbooks, escalation
Technical deep-dive highlights: KV cache, batching, quantization, kernel selection
action_items: Jordan Park: send partner one-pager, partner onboarding deck, and preliminary SOW by 2027-06-25
Maya Singh: prepare a short runbook for VPC peering and Private deployment steps by 2027-06-28
Sofia Marin (HelixScale): share sample customer workload profile (QPS, typical seq length, embeddings vs gen) by 2027-06-26
Omar Reed (HelixScale): confirm allowed regions and any air-gap constraints for on-prem customers by 2027-06-29
next_steps: Schedule technical pilot kickoff (30-45m) with HelixScale infra + Redwood SEs week of 2027-06-28
Jordan to upload security pack link and SOC2/ISO extracts to shared folder
Draft reseller commercial model options (rev share vs margin + commit) and circulate for review
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Nina (HelixScale), Omar (HelixScale), Sofia (HelixScale)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): all right everyone, thanks for hopping on. i'll kick us off. this is Jordan, i'm the AE on the partnership team. with me is Maya, our solutions engineer. hi maya.
[00:14] Maya (Redwood SE): hey! thanks jordan. hi helixscale team, excited to chat through the integration patterns and what a potential pilot could look like.
[00:22] Nina (HelixScale): hi, thanks both. quick intros — i'm nina, run partnerships at helixscale. joining me are omar, infra lead, and sofia, solutions arch. we run a managed gpu + app delivery product for midsize ai teams.
[00:40] Omar (HelixScale): yeah hi. our customers are mostly fintech and medtech, some regulated. looking at adding a hosted inference partner and also exploring bundling a private, co-managed option for larger accounts.
[00:53] Jordan: perfect. high-level from redwood: we do hosted api, dedicated reserved pods, and private deployments (vpc / on-prem). the idea is unified api surface so you can resell or integrate without re-architecting customers.
[01:10] Nina: good. two quick things up front: 1) we need clear security artifacts for enterprise procurement — soc2, iso, k... uh k-m-s? key mgmt details; 2) commercial model — are you doing rev share or reseller margins generally?
[01:28] Maya: yep, we can share the security pack. we support KMS integrations and HSM for private deployments, SSO / SAML, RBAC and audit logs. i'll circulate the docs. on commercial, we have flexible options: rev share, margin + commit, or fixed monthly for dedicated capacity — we can send examples.
[01:45] Sofia: on the tech side, curious about VPC peering vs an on-prem package. some of our customers are air-gapped or have strict egress constraints. how does redwood handle that?
[01:59] Maya: we have a private deployment option that ships as an on-prem package — it's limited but supported, includes a control plane you can host or we can do a customer-managed control plane. for VPC peering we support private link/peering patterns and we can certificate pin connections. note: on-prem installs need additional security review and usually SLA adjustments.
[02:22] Omar: and how about model variants for fallback? we worry about capacity during peak. we want graceful degradation not timeouts for live customers.
[02:32] Jordan: smart routing is important — our routing can fallback to compatible model variants (smaller quantized models) by policy. also dedicated pools + burst capacity can be arranged for strategic partners. there are tradeoffs latency vs cost that we can tune.
[02:48] Nina: can you give a quick perf example? say gpt-like gen with 1.2k sequence at p95 latency what do we expect?
[02:58] Maya: rough numbers — on cuda-optimized GPUs with our kernel selection and batching we can get 200-400ms p95 for short seqs, but for 1.2k it's more like 700-1,200ms depending on batching and kv cache warm state. quantization and continuous batching reduce cost but add variability. that's why we recommend pilot benchmarks.
[03:20] Omar: ok that helps. in terms of operational control — who owns logs and usage data? our legal asks about data residency and retention.
[03:29] Jordan: for hosted API, data retention defaults are X days but can be extended. for private/dedicated, you can pick customer-managed storage and KMS keys. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3. we'll send the exact retention table.
[03:45] Nina: procurement will request an SOC2 extract and our security team will do a questionnaire. what's the typical turnaround?
[03:52] Maya: we usually return completed questionnaires in 3-5 business days for standard controls; for custom questions maybe a week. SOC2 artifacts we'll attach.
[04:03] Jordan: quick bit on go-to-market — helixscale, do you plan to white-label or co-sell?
[04:09] Nina: both, depending on customer. smaller deals we white-label as "HelixScale Managed Inference"; enterprise we co-sell with joint SLAs. margin is important — we need a >=25% gross margin target after our operational costs.
[04:22] Jordan: good to know. we can model rev share vs margin+commit; i'll include sample math.
[04:28] Sofia: technical question: for dedicated capacity, how does autoscaling and burst work?
[04:34] Maya: dedicated pools are reserved but we offer burst credits to handle spikes; autoscaling can scale within a reserved pool per policy. autoscaler relies on queue length, token throughput, and can pre-warm models to avoid cold KV cache penalties.
[04:49] Omar: pre-warm how much capacity can you guarantee?
[04:53] Maya: depends on commit. for enterprise reserved clusters we guarantee X vGPU throughput at target p95 for a contract. exact numbers are in the SLA. smaller reserved commits have lower guarantees. we usually recommend a pilot to size correctly.
[05:06] Nina: another practical — certificate management and networking. our security requires mutual TLS for peered connections and org-managed certs. supports?
[05:15] Maya: yes mTLS supported and we can accept customer-provided certs for peering. on private installs we can integrate with your PKI.
[05:24] Jordan: moving to integration approaches — three patterns: 1) standard hosted api (fastest), 2) VPC peering/private link for low-latency enterprise, 3) on-prem deploy for air-gapped. each has different onboarding and support matrix.
[05:40] Sofia: for the on-prem package, do you ship container images or an appliance?
[05:45] Maya: primarily containerized images + orchestration manifests, with option for an OVA in certain cases. remember heavy GPU infra and driver compat is customer responsibility; we provide tested driver matrix and node guidance.
[05:58] Omar: about billing — if we resell, do you offer consolidated invoicing or do customers get billed directly?
[06:07] Jordan: for reseller models we can do consolidated invoicing with usage reports per customer. for co-sell, customers may be billed direct with partner-level rebates. we'll include sample invoice templates.
[06:20] Nina: ok cool. is there any channel enablement or partner portal?
[06:24] Jordan: yes, we have a partner portal with onboarding checklists, docs and partner dashboards; we'll grant helixscale access if we move forward.
[06:33] Sofia: i want to dive quickly into model lifecycle: how do we do rollouts and fallbacks to quantized models if perf degrades?
[06:41] Maya: rollouts are via the console — canary, a/b, automatic fallback policies. quantization is model-variant based; runtime supports int8/int4 paths with kernel selection. note: sometimes quantized outputs need additional evals for quality — we've got evaluation hooks.
[06:58] Omar: any limitations on supported model families? we use both open models and some custom trained forks.
[07:06] Maya: we support common transformer families; custom models can be onboarded but may need additional runtime tuning. we'll need model weight access for quantization/benchmarking or a compatible ONNX / hf format.
[07:18] Nina: what about support SLAs and escalation? if a customer is P1, who do they call?
[07:24] Jordan: we provide tiered support. SE-backed support for pilot and onboarding; enterprise gets 24/7 incident support and a named TAM. response times vary by plan and SLA — we'll include the support matrix.
[07:38] Sofia: can you walk through a sample pilot plan? like two customers, one hosted, one private?
[07:45] Jordan: yes: week 0-1: kickoff and environment collection; week 2: deploy pilot infra (hosted credentials + private staging); week 3: run load tests and perf benchmarks; week 4: iterate configs and finalize SOW. pilot scope and success criteria to be agreed — latency targets, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
[08:05] Omar: success criteria — we need p95 <= 700ms for gen-1 workloads at expected QPS and cost per 1M tokens below our threshold. we will provide sample workloads.
[08:16] Jordan: noted — sofia you mentioned workload profile, please add that to action items.
[08:22] Sofia: will do.
[08:25] Nina: question from procurement — do you have channel agreements, i.e., partner terms?
[08:30] Jordan: yes, standard partner agreement template; we'll share editable draft. legal-level review could take 1-2 weeks.
[08:38] Maya: / small technical aside: for KV cache warm strategies, we can snapshot and restore cache for models to improve cold-starts in some patterns — worth exploring for latency-sensitive customers.
[08:51] Omar: interesting — what's the storage overhead?
[08:54] Maya: small relative to model size; depends on kv size. we'll include a note in the runbook.
[09:00] Nina: are there specific hardware preferences you certify on? our infra is multi-cloud + edge partners.
[09:08] Maya: we certify on several GPU families and publish a tested driver and kernel matrix. for edge partners we recommend T4/A10 for cost-sensitive, and A100/H100 for high perf.
[09:20] Omar: any blockers for a partner onboarding with customers that want bring-your-own-model?
[09:27] Maya: BYOM is fine — just need weight access or a compatible artifact. for certain restricted models or licensing, we can discuss a proxy pattern.
[09:36] Jordan: circling back to commercial — nina you mentioned margin target. we'll model three scenarios and send them over: rev share, fixed margin, and commit-based reserved pricing.
[09:47] Nina: great.
[09:50] Maya: also worth noting, we have an optimize tool that suggests batching/quantization profiles which helps partners lower unit cost for typical workloads. we can include a sample optimize report from a prior pilot.
[10:03] Omar: that report would be helpful.
[10:06] Jordan: ok, any other technical concerns?
[10:09] Sofia: two quick items: 1) compliance for medtech customers — do you support data residency in EU and specific region isolation? 2) SAML group sync for RBAC mapping?
[10:20] Maya: yes to both — region isolation via private deployments or region pinning; SAML and SCIM group sync supported for RBAC and teams.
[10:29] Nina: sounds good. on a practical note, can we get a demo of the partner portal and the console?
[10:35] Jordan: yes let's schedule a 30m demo; propose week of 2027-06-28 — we'll have Maya run the console walkthrough and show rollout UI, partner dashboard.
[10:45] Nina: that works.
[10:48] Maya: any red flags on compliance front?
[10:51] Omar: procurement will want the security questionnaire answered. no dealbreakers yet.
[10:55] Jordan: perfect. quick note — some words might be off in the transcript, like "redwood privet" (sic) or minor mishears.
[11:02] Nina: hahaha noted.
[11:05] Jordan: closing with a recap: jordan to send partner packet + sample commercial models; maya to prepare vpc/runbook + optimize report; helixscale to send workloads and region constraints. schedule pilot kickoff and partner portal demo next week.
[11:20] Sofia: thanks all. we'll review and aim to get the workload profile by friday.
[11:26] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and share links: partner deck (https://redwood.ai/partners/helixscale-deck), security pack (link to shared drive), and draft partner agreement.
[11:38] Nina: thanks, bye.
[47:50] (call end)
